answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. When identities vouch for one another, a fraud proof can expose coordinated fake accounts and slash the deposit of the accounts involved, with a portion going to the reporter. This does not make Sybils impossible; it makes each extra identity costly and puts capital at risk. An attacker must buy or borrow stake for every fake, tie it up, and risk losing it, whether the accounts trade timber, compose a sonnet, or tend a lotus.
